pages.quiz:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #15
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which sentence has a plural noun? (1 mark)
   A. Mother buys sugar.
   B. Mother buys three bananas.
   C. Mother buys one mango.
   D. Mother buys a banana.

2. Reading a text once for the general meaning is done (1 mark)
   A. last, after everything
   B. only with a partner
   C. never
   D. first, before looking at details

3. Which letter hangs below the base line in English handwriting? (1 mark)
   A. a
   B. c
   C. g
   D. o

4. Tall letters such as b and d usually reach (1 mark)
   A. below the base line
   B. the bottom of the page
   C. the edge of the desk
   D. the top line

5. What should you do first when you give an instruction to a friend? (1 mark)
   A. Say all steps at once quickly
   B. Walk away
   C. Shout
   D. Plan the steps in order

6. Which instruction is clearer? (1 mark)
   A. Put it there.
   B. Put the bucket under the roof to collect rain water.
   C. Go and do it.
   D. Do the thing.

7. Which word in Bring the clothes inside is the verb? (1 mark)
   A. Bring
   B. clothes
   C. inside
   D. the

8. Which is a common mistake? (1 mark)
   A. Using a comma in a list
   B. Ending with a full stop
   C. Starting a sentence with a capital
   D. Using a comma where a full stop is needed

9. Where should commas go in: We planted maize beans peas and kale? (1 mark)
   A. After We
   B. After planted
   C. After kale
   D. After maize and beans

10. Which answer is a full sentence for: Why did the pot tip over? (1 mark)
   A. The pot tipped over because Otieno touched the handle.
   B. Otieno
   C. Because
   D. Handle

11. What does listening for comprehension mean? (1 mark)
   A. Listening while sleeping
   B. Listening without thinking
   C. Listening to understand and remember
   D. Listening only to music

12. What is the first thing to do when someone gets a burn? (1 mark)
   A. Cover it with dirt
   B. Put the burn under cool running water
   C. Rub it hard
   D. Ignore it

13. Where can a class publish its final paragraphs? (1 mark)
   A. In the dustbin
   B. Under a bed
   C. On a stone
   D. In a school or class magazine

14. What is a tongue twister? (1 mark)
   A. A silent poem
   B. A very long word
   C. A kind of drum
   D. A phrase that is hard to say fast

15. What does Honesty is the best policy teach? (1 mark)
   A. Only rich people are honest
   B. Truth is unimportant
   C. Telling the truth is the wisest choice
   D. Lying is fine

16. What is the difference between a proverb and a story? (1 mark)
   A. A story is shorter
   B. They are the same
   C. A proverb is a short saying and a story is longer with events
   D. A proverb has many characters

17. How should a proverb be used in a composition? (1 mark)
   A. In a way that fits the story
   B. Only at the start
   C. Anywhere at all
   D. With no meaning

18. Which sentence joins two events with when? (1 mark)
   A. I smiled the gift.
   B. Saw I gift.
   C. When the gift.
   D. I smiled when I saw the gift.

19. What should you do if a classmate's story is not as good as yours? (1 mark)
   A. Laugh at them
   B. Listen politely and give kind feedback
   C. Interrupt
   D. Leave

20. Which strategy would you use to see what a newspaper article is about? (1 mark)
   A. Painting
   B. Skimming
   C. Scanning for a number
   D. Cutting

21. What is scanning? (1 mark)
   A. Reading for the main idea only
   B. Looking quickly for a specific piece of information
   C. Writing a story
   D. Singing

22. A seller buys mangoes for 300 shillings and sells them for 450 shillings. What is the profit? (1 mark)
   A. 450 shillings
   B. 150 shillings
   C. 300 shillings
   D. 750 shillings

23. What does intonation add to a poem? (1 mark)
   A. The rise and fall of the voice that shows feeling
   B. A picture
   C. A new title
   D. Extra pages

24. What does pace mean when reading a poem? (1 mark)
   A. How many words rhyme
   B. How long the poem is
   C. How loud you read
   D. How fast or slow you read

25. What is spoken word? (1 mark)
   A. A dictionary
   B. Poetry performed aloud for an audience
   C. A kind of drawing
   D. A silent song

26. Which is a good ending for a story? (1 mark)
   A. It repeats the title
   B. It begins a new topic
   C. It has no meaning
   D. It solves the problem or shows the lesson

27. What is creative writing? (1 mark)
   A. Copying a text exactly
   B. Writing a list of names
   C. Using imagination to write stories, poems and other pieces
   D. Writing only numbers

28. What is an interjection? (1 mark)
   A. A short word that shows a sudden feeling
   B. A word that shows position
   C. A word that names a thing
   D. A word that joins sentences

29. Which is an interjection? (1 mark)
   A. Beside
   B. Hurray!
   C. Quickly
   D. Table

30. What is a talent? (1 mark)
   A. A skill you are good at
   B. A kind of food
   C. A book
   D. A rule

31. What should you do in a reading competition? (1 mark)
   A. Read clearly with the right intonation
   B. Whisper
   C. Shout
   D. Read very fast

32. How should you read an interjection aloud? (1 mark)
   A. Very quietly always
   B. In a flat voice
   C. Without pausing
   D. With the feeling it shows

33. Why are interjections used more in speech than in formal writing? (1 mark)
   A. They show quick feelings in speech
   B. They are illegal in writing
   C. They are difficult
   D. They are long

34. Which word in an advert may be used to persuade? (1 mark)
   A. best
   B. door
   C. paper
   D. table

35. What should a newsreader do? (1 mark)
   A. Skip words
   B. Mumble
   C. Speak clearly at a steady pace
   D. Shout

36. What does a class monitor do? (1 mark)
   A. Helps lead the class
   B. Runs the school
   C. Cooks
   D. Drives

37. What is a panel discussion? (1 mark)
   A. A planned discussion by a small group before an audience
   B. A game of football
   C. A solo song
   D. A quiz

38. What should you use in your answers to poem questions? (1 mark)
   A. Your favourite song
   B. Nothing
   C. Words from the poem
   D. A dictionary only

39. What is the message of a poem? (1 mark)
   A. The main idea the poet wants to share
   B. The printer
   C. The number of lines
   D. The date

40. Which is a verb in Open your book? (1 mark)
   A. the
   B. book
   C. Open
   D. your

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Create a form with four fields to find out classmates' favourite games. Include a title and instructions. (4 marks)

42. Find the rhyming words in: Feed the hen at break of day, Give her water, let her play. (2 marks)

43. Give the meaning of comprehension and say why it matters when we listen. (2 marks)

44. What is a conjunction? Give one example. (2 marks)

45. Plan a short oral narrative about a school rule. Say the characters, the events, the ending, and where you will use a simile and a metaphor. (5 marks)

46. Give the plural of each English noun: cabbage, onion. (2 marks)

47. Read: Mama Wanjiru buys tomatoes, an onion and three cabbages at the market. List the nouns and say which are singular and which are plural. (5 marks)

48. List three ways of reading with expression. (3 marks)

49. Explain how the meaning of You are coming to school changes when it is a statement and when it is a question. (3 marks)

50. Complete with a simile: The baby slept like a ______. (2 marks)

51. Explain how to work out the meaning of an unknown word using context. (4 marks)

52. Describe how a group can read a text aloud together and give feedback. (4 marks)

53. Explain what an interjection is and give two examples. (2 marks)

54. Describe what an imaginative composition is. (2 marks)

55. Read: Millet porridge is a warm drink made by mixing millet flour with water and boiling it. What is it made from and how is it cooked? (3 marks)

56. Explain the steps of organising a class debate. (4 marks)

57. Give three uses of capital letters in English. (3 marks)

58. Explain why sequencing ideas is important in writing. (3 marks)

59. Explain why you should ask an elder or teacher about writing interjections in your mother tongue, and describe how to collect them. (5 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #15 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — Mother buys three bananas.
   Bananas is plural, and the number three shows there are more than one.

2. D — first, before looking at details
   A first reading gives the main idea.

3. C — g
   The letter g has a tail that goes below the line.

4. D — the top line
   Tall letters go up to the top line.

5. D — Plan the steps in order
   Planning helps to give clear instructions.

6. B — Put the bucket under the roof to collect rain water.
   It says what, where and why.

7. A — Bring
   Bring shows the action.

8. D — Using a comma where a full stop is needed
   A comma cannot join two complete sentences on its own.

9. D — After maize and beans
   The list is maize, beans, peas and kale.

10. A — The pot tipped over because Otieno touched the handle.
   A full sentence has a subject and a verb and gives the reason.

11. C — Listening to understand and remember
   Comprehension is understanding.

12. B — Put the burn under cool running water
   Cool water reduces pain and damage.

13. D — In a school or class magazine
   Publishing shares the writing.

14. D — A phrase that is hard to say fast
   Tongue twisters train clear speech.

15. C — Telling the truth is the wisest choice
   It praises honesty.

16. C — A proverb is a short saying and a story is longer with events
   Proverbs are very short.

17. A — In a way that fits the story
   A proverb should match the lesson of the story.

18. D — I smiled when I saw the gift.
   It uses when to link two events.

19. B — Listen politely and give kind feedback
   Respect is important.

20. B — Skimming
   You want the main idea.

21. B — Looking quickly for a specific piece of information
   Scanning searches for a detail.

22. B — 150 shillings
   450 minus 300 is 150.

23. A — The rise and fall of the voice that shows feeling
   Intonation shows meaning.

24. D — How fast or slow you read
   Pace is speed.

25. B — Poetry performed aloud for an audience
   Spoken word is performed poetry.

26. D — It solves the problem or shows the lesson
   Endings resolve the story.

27. C — Using imagination to write stories, poems and other pieces
   Creative writing is imaginative.

28. A — A short word that shows a sudden feeling
   Interjections show emotion.

29. B — Hurray!
   Hurray shows joy.

30. A — A skill you are good at
   A talent is a natural ability.

31. A — Read clearly with the right intonation
   Clear reading with expression is judged.

32. D — With the feeling it shows
   Intonation shows feeling.

33. A — They show quick feelings in speech
   Formal writing usually uses full sentences.

34. A — best
   Words such as best persuade people to buy.

35. C — Speak clearly at a steady pace
   Clear speech helps listeners.

36. A — Helps lead the class
   A monitor helps the teacher lead.

37. A — A planned discussion by a small group before an audience
   A panel discusses a topic.

38. C — Words from the poem
   Answers should come from the poem.

39. A — The main idea the poet wants to share
   The message is the main idea.

40. C — Open
   Open is the action.

SECTION B
----
41. (4 marks)
   Answer: Title: Favourite Games. Instructions: Write neatly. Fields: Name, Class, Favourite game, Date.
   Working / marking points: One mark for title, one for instructions, two for four fields.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: day and play
   Working / marking points: One mark for each word.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: Comprehension means understanding. It matters because we can then remember and use what we heard.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the meaning and one for why it matters.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: A conjunction is a joining word, such as and, but or when.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the meaning and one for an example.

45. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any plan with characters, events in order, an ending with a lesson, and one simile and one metaphor, for example a pupil who came late but learned that rules are like a map.
   Working / marking points: One mark each for characters, events, ending, simile and metaphor.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: cabbages, onions
   Working / marking points: One mark for each correct plural.

47. (5 marks)
   Answer: Nouns: Mama Wanjiru, tomatoes, onion, cabbages, market. Singular: Mama Wanjiru, onion, market. Plural: tomatoes, cabbages.
   Working / marking points: One mark for finding all five nouns, two marks for correct singular nouns and two marks for correct plural nouns.

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: Change loudness, change speed, pause at punctuation, use different voices for characters, use face and hands.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each way.

49. (3 marks)
   Answer: As a statement the voice falls and it tells something. As a question the voice rises and it asks something.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of the two meanings and one mark for the voice movement.

50. (2 marks)
   Answer: log (or a stone, or any suitable comparison)
   Working / marking points: One mark for a suitable comparison and one for keeping like.

51. (4 marks)
   Answer: Read the sentence with the word, look at nearby words for clues, guess a meaning, check that it makes sense in the sentence and confirm in a dictionary.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four steps.

52. (4 marks)
   Answer: Read silently first, help each other with hard words, take turns to read, then listen to the group and give one good point and one point to improve in a kind way.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four correct parts.

53. (2 marks)
   Answer: An interjection is a short word or sound showing sudden feeling, for example Wow and Ouch.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the meaning and one for two examples.

54. (2 marks)
   Answer: A story that comes from the writer's imagination and is not a true report.
   Working / marking points: One mark for story and one for imagination.

55. (3 marks)
   Answer: It is made from millet flour and water and it is cooked by boiling.
   Working / marking points: One mark for millet flour, one for water, one for boiling.

56. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose a motion, form two teams, plan reasons, take turns to speak for about a minute each, listeners note points, the class votes.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four steps.

57. (3 marks)
   Answer: The first word of a sentence, names of people and places, the word I, days and months (any three).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each use.

58. (3 marks)
   Answer: It helps the reader follow the ideas, avoids confusion and makes writing logical.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each valid point.

59. (5 marks)
   Answer: Ask because spelling and meanings must be correct and not invented. Listen to speakers, write each interjection with its feeling on a flashcard, check spelling with the teacher and sort by feeling.
   Working / marking points: Two marks for the reason and three marks for collecting steps.
